verdict.rationale: Lium is a GPU rental marketplace whose evidence shows only building blocks for automation: an API and CLI an external agent can drive, pod TTLs and spend caps that auto-delete pods, and an SDK that runs a single function on a rented node. There is no documented first-party feature for setting up recurring, scheduled or triggered automations that run on their own in the background. The autonomy described in the evidence lives in the user's own agent, and auto-removal is a one-off lifecycle control rather than an automation system.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background
